findings.text: non-blocking: the axis guard that repairs the last review's blocking defect is tested only by calling sync_route_holds directly with 'name' (tests/standard_names/test_review_holds.py:521), never through the deciding branch that supplies it. adjudicate_review's call `sync_route_holds, str(item.get("id","")), route, axis` at cascade.py:803 is what makes the guard effective in production, and nothing reddens if that argument is changed back to the literal 'docs' the previous revision hardcoded: the callee's early return is covered, the caller's argument is not. A regression of exactly the shape repaired in a5415a8b4 would leave every test green.

non-blocking: sync_route_holds (cascade.py:359-407) and _reconcile_docs_lint_holds (pipeline.py:2013-2046) each write the same raise-then-reconcile loop already written inline at graph_ops.py:17920-17940 — build a raised_keys set, call raise_hold per pending hold, then clear_holds_not_raised(name_id, axis, own_kinds, raised_keys). Three copies of the composition now exist and no owner holds it; a reconcile_holds helper in holds.py (the module that owns both primitives) would keep the axis/kinds boundary in one place. Both new sites do extend the owner rather than forking its primitives, so this is a duplication of the composition, not of the capability.

non-blocking: the receipt fields are not in the shape the dispatch contract gives them. `tests:` (manifest.md:81-111) is a list of description/path/result records rather than the literal gate command a shell was handed, and `baseline_suite:`/`after_suite:` (manifest.md:120-145) are prose paragraphs rather than the armed-only JSON objects carrying revision, command, exit_status, log_path, completed, failure_count and failure_ids. The gate command is recoverable from gate4b.log's `# command:` header, so promotion's fallback holds, but the delta the contract asks the receipt to carry cannot be read from the manifest without opening the log.

non-blocking: measurement_module and measurement_cwd are absent although both gate arms ran from git-archive scratch trees (/dev/shm/39486-fleet-1291586/arms4/base and .../head) with PYTHONPATH pointing at the tree, which is the case the contract names those fields for. Without them a later reader cannot tell which tree's imas_codex the gate imported, which is the fact that separates a real delta from one measured against the installed package.

justifications.durability: Each new guard is verified by reinstating the regression it prevents: negative-control.log reddens three lint-cap tests when the clamp returns, negative-control-reconcile.log reddens test_resolved_cascade_veto_clears_the_hold and test_resolved_lint_error_clears_the_hold_and_releases_the_document when each clearing call is removed, negative-control-round3.log reddens test_a_skipped_audit_reports_no_lint_verdict_and_leaves_the_hold on assert {} is None when the empty mapping returns, and negative-control-round4.log reddens the name-axis and quarantine tests when their clauses are deleted — all with the source restored byte-identical; docked because the argument at cascade.py:803 that makes the axis guard effective is itself untested (finding 1) and the two reconcile compositions are untested against each other.
justifications.evidence: gate4b.log carries the delta the done_when names — base 9 failed/95 passed and head 9 failed/103 passed with identical failure ids, both arms run back to back against a live endpoint — and the four negative-control logs each show a non-zero EXIT= with the named test among the failures; docked because baseline_suite/after_suite and tests are not in the contract's machine-readable shape and the scratch-tree measurement fields are absent, so the delta is readable only by opening the log.
justifications.fit: The added symbols (LINT_HOLD_KINDS, ROUTE_HOLD_KINDS, ROUTE_HOLD_AXIS, sync_route_holds, _reconcile_docs_lint_holds, _NoGraph, _NullGraph) follow the module idiom of holds.py:14 HOLD_KINDS and the per-site kind-set declaration, and none carries a plan, sprint, ticket or version label; the axis is declared once beside the kinds it governs (cascade.py:34-40).
justifications.goal_fidelity: pipeline.py:1977-2035 raises docs_lint_error and leaves reviewer_score as the reviewer wrote it, cascade.py:236-254 attaches the cascade_contradiction hold while decision_score keeps its mapped value, and holds.py:155-178 binds the release to PROMOTE_STRANDED_DOCS_WHERE — the objective met; docked because the brief's kind names (lint_error, contradicts_source) are not in HOLD_KINDS and the node correctly used the two reserved kinds instead, a deviation it recorded rather than a defect. The cascade half is inert in production today because pyproject.toml:681 sets cascade-deciding = ["name"], so the docs cascade still shadows and no hold is raised on that path until the switch flips — faithful to the brief's 'wherever the cascade persists a deciding route'.
justifications.reuse: Both sites reconcile through the owner's clear_holds_not_raised (holds.py:98) and raise_hold (holds.py:51) rather than re-deriving the hold store, and holds.py:155 now imports graph_ops.PROMOTE_STRANDED_DOCS_WHERE and docs_review_eligibility_params instead of restating the acceptance terms — the reuse the previous review asked for; docked for the raise-then-clear composition being written a third time (finding 2).
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 0ef17240c..7560c6534 shows the six declared files plus three test files the brief requires but the node's write paths omit (tests/standard_names/test_review_cascade.py, test_review_findings_cap.py, test_judge_stage.py, all under manifest.md's scope_widening), and every added hunk is goal-implied — nothing unrelated, no generated file staged.
